extracted.intended_audience: book publishers, imprint editorial staff, and acquisitions teams submitting titles to Kirkus Reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for publishers on which books Kirkus Reviews will consider, how and when to submit digital galleys/PDFs, section contacts, and exclusions. Focused on pre-publication review submissions for trade and children/YA titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus will consider titles that are submitted as digital galleys or e-books at least 4-5 months before publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As soon as a book is reviewed—usually 2-3 months before its publication date—the publisher is notified of the review rundate. These timing guidelines are intended to help get the right titles into the right hands at the right time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit only digital galleys and PDFs for review consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact individual section editors for further details, but in most cases we request an open widget on NetGalley or Edelweiss plus a PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible title types / formats
rubrics_metrics.description: We consider all new adult hardcover or original trade-paperback fiction, general-audience nonfiction, and children’s and teen books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors make individual judgments about coverage based on merit or potential interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories not reviewed in the traditional program
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus does not review books in the categories listed below in its traditional program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded categories (verbatim list): —already published books —reprints of books that Kirkus has previously reviewed —self-published titles —print-on-demand titles —poetry (except children’s and teen) —cookbooks —crafting books —guidebooks, including travel guides —personal finance —textbooks —specialized technical or professional works —any work intended primarily for an academic audience —reference books —instruction or how-to manuals —screenplays or other dramatic scripts —computer and technology handbooks —books of regional interest. Note: Kirkus Indie does not put genre or publication date limits on submissions (see Kirkus Indie for exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher-submitted requirement and hybrid-publisher eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles must be submitted by the publisher; books from hybrid publishers with a national distributor are eligible for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title must be submitted by the publisher (hybrid publishers eligible only if they have a national distributor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section contacts and submission routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit to the appropriate section editor or generic section email for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiction: Laurie Muchnick, lmuchnick@kirkus.com; send submissions for Laurie to fiction@kirkus.com. Nonfiction: John McMurtrie, jmcmurtrie@kirkus.com; send submissions for John to nonfiction@kirkus.com. Young Readers: Laura Simeon, lsimeon@kirkus.com — middle grade (209 pages and longer) and young adult. Mahnaz Dar, mdar@kirkus.com — board books, picture books, and middle grade (through 208 pages). Please send submissions for Mahnaz to kidsubs@kirkus.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage is limited and discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus receives between 100 and 200 submissions per day, and we’re not able to review every title we receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines are intended to help publishers get the right titles into the right hands at the right time so they can receive consideration; ultimately editors make individual judgments about coverage based on merit or potential interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kirkus Indie program exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Indie does not put genre or publication date limits on submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For titles not eligible under the traditional program (for example many self-published books), see Kirkus Indie for submission options and different rules.
